units.title: Discovery of the Orally Bioavailable Isoform Selective Janus Kinase 1 (JAK1) Compound Povorcitinib (INCB054707) for the Treatment of Inflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases
units.text: Sparing JAK2 is the whole point: inhibit it and you take the patient's blood counts with you.

units.title: The disease
units.text: Autoimmune and inflammatory disease, where signalling runs predominantly through JAK1 heterodimers. The approved dual JAK1/JAK2 inhibitors work, and their JAK2 activity brings anaemia and other cytopenias with it.

units.title: The selectivity problem
units.text: JAK2 supports haematopoiesis, so inhibiting it costs the patient red cells and platelets. The four JAK family kinases share a highly conserved ATP site, and the two isoforms in question differ subtly enough that the paper's own selectivity explanation is offered as a hypothesis rather than a result.

units.title: The property problem
units.text: This campaign is almost entirely a pharmacokinetics story. Potency was adequate early; oral exposure was not, and the dog was where every candidate failed until the hinge binder itself was replaced.

units.title: Inhibit JAK2 and you take the blood counts with you
units.text: The approved dual JAK1/JAK2 inhibitors work in inflammatory disease, and their JAK2 activity brings anaemia and other cytopenias with it, because JAK2 carries the signals that maintain haematopoiesis. Autoimmune and inflammatory signalling runs predominantly through JAK1 heterodimers, so a JAK1-selective inhibitor should keep the benefit and leave blood cell production alone. The difficulty is that the four JAK kinases share a highly conserved ATP site, and the campaign's own starting candidate, itacitinib, managed only 21-fold.

units.title: Inhibit JAK2 and you take the blood counts with you
units.text: Drugs of this class already work for inflammatory disease. The problem is that they also block a near-identical enzyme the body uses to make blood cells, so patients can become anaemic. The aim here was to block one and not the other. That is hard, because the two enzymes are nearly the same shape where the drug binds, and the company's previous attempt managed only a twenty-fold preference.

units.title: The scaffold that first bought selectivity
units.text: The urea capping group of the early scaffold was holding the ADME back. Replacing it with a phenyl amide improved potency and took Caco-2 from 0.3 to 2.1; shrinking the piperidine to an azetidine added three-fold more through rigidity. Opening the methylpyrrolidine to a simple isopropyl amide then brought projected human clearance to 0.7 L/h/kg, removed a metabolic liability, held potency at 1.6 nM, and doubled whole blood isoform selectivity to 12-fold. That is compound 9, and its dog pharmacokinetics were worse than itacitinib's.

units.title: The scaffold that first bought selectivity
units.text: Three changes in a row, each simplifying the molecule: a different chemical group at one end, a smaller and more rigid ring in the middle, and then opening a ring into something simpler still. Potency held, the liver slowed down, and the margin over the enzyme to avoid doubled. Then the compound was given to dogs, where it did worse than the drug it was meant to beat.

units.title: One fluorine, and the compound learns to cross membranes
units.text: An ortho-fluorine lets the amide N-H fold back into an intramolecular hydrogen bond, masking polar surface and lifting Caco-2 three-fold with a four-fold gain in rat exposure. Adding the trifluoromethyl on top gave compound 16: Caco-2 up five-fold and cynomolgus exposure up 52-fold against compound 9. The trifluoromethyl alone, without the ortho-fluorine, did essentially nothing, so the two changes only work together. The tactic was not new here: the same trick had produced an approved c-Met inhibitor and a clinical 11-beta-HSD1 inhibitor in earlier in-house programmes.

units.title: One fluorine, and the compound learns to cross membranes
units.text: A single fluorine atom, placed beside the amide, lets the molecule tuck one of its own polar ends against itself. Hidden that way it slips through membranes far more easily, and fifty times more of it reached the bloodstream of a monkey. The same fluorine added on its own to a different position did nothing: the two changes only pay together.

units.title: Take the fluorine off again and watch it fall over
units.text: Compound 19 is compound 18 with the ortho-fluorine removed and nothing else changed. Enzymatic potency is identical at 0.25 nM. Caco-2 falls from 8.5 to 1.4, rat exposure from 11,884 to 5,606 nM.h, rat bioavailability from 54 to 21 per cent. That is the difference between a hypothesis about an intramolecular hydrogen bond and a demonstration of one, and it costs a single atom to run.

units.title: Take the fluorine off again and watch it fall over
units.text: To prove the fluorine was doing what they thought, the chemists made the same molecule without it. It was exactly as potent and far worse at everything else: six times less able to cross a membrane, half the exposure in an animal. Undoing a change and watching the benefit vanish is the cleanest evidence in this whole set of four papers.

units.title: Giving away 44-fold to fix the dog
units.text: The pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidine hinge binder is electron-rich and prone to CYP oxidation, so it was replaced by a 3,5-dimethylpyrazole: 44-fold weaker on the enzyme, nearly twice as isoform-selective at 46-fold, and in beagle dogs clearance fell from 82 to 4 per cent of hepatic blood flow with oral bioavailability rising from 1 to 100 per cent. Povorcitinib was then crystallised in both JAK1 and JAK2, the only true twin structure in this set. The hinge contacts to Glu930 and Leu932 are identical in both. The authors attribute the selectivity to JAK1's P-loop sitting about 2 A higher, opening a lipophilic groove for the trifluoromethyl, with JAK2's Asn859, Phe860 and Glu1015 closing that space, and they state plainly that this is speculative.

units.title: Giving away 44-fold to fix the dog
units.text: The last change replaced the part that grips the protein with something smaller and harder for the body to destroy. It cost a great deal of raw potency and fixed the dog completely: a compound that had been almost entirely destroyed before absorption now arrived intact. The drug was then crystallised in both proteins, the one it should block and the one it should spare. It grips both identically at the hinge, and the explanation for its preference lies around the edges of the pocket, which the chemists are careful to call a hypothesis.

units.title: Urea out, phenyl amide in
units.text: The urea was suspected of the poor ADME. Replacing the azetidine with a phenyl and the urea with an amide doubled enzymatic potency to 3.3 nM, improved cellular potency nearly three-fold and took Caco-2 from 0.3 to 2.1.

units.title: Urea out, phenyl amide in
units.text: The first scaffold had a chemical group that was holding its properties back. Swapping it for a flat ring made the compound both more potent and far better at crossing membranes.

units.title: Piperidine to azetidine
units.text: Exchanging the six-membered piperidine for the more conformationally rigid four-membered azetidine gave about three-fold on enzyme and cell and two-fold in whole blood, with permeability holding.

units.title: Piperidine to azetidine
units.text: Shrinking one ring from six atoms to four made the molecule more rigid and three times more potent. Rigidity is a recurring theme: it costs the molecule fewer options and it pays.

units.title: Breaking the ring to a secondary amide
units.text: Opening the methylpyrrolidine to a simple isopropyl amide introduced the polarity needed to bring projected human clearance down to 0.7 L/h/kg, removed a metabolically vulnerable methyl, held potency, and unexpectedly doubled whole blood isoform selectivity to 12-fold.

units.title: Breaking the ring to a secondary amide
units.text: Opening one ring into a simpler group did three things at once: it slowed the liver down, removed a spot the body liked to attack, and doubled the margin over the isoform that must be left alone.

units.title: One fluorine, folded into a hydrogen bond
units.text: An ortho-fluorine lets the amide N-H fold back into an intramolecular hydrogen bond, masking the polar surface that was blocking permeability. Caco-2 rises three-fold, rat exposure four-fold and rat bioavailability two-fold. The tactic came from two earlier in-house programmes on entirely different targets.

units.title: One fluorine, folded into a hydrogen bond
units.text: A single fluorine atom, placed next to the amide, lets the molecule tuck one of its own polar groups against itself. Hidden that way, it slips through membranes far more easily. Four times as much of it reached the bloodstream.

units.title: The trifluoromethyl only works with the fluorine
units.text: Adding the trifluoromethyl to the ortho-fluorinated amide gave Caco-2 of 4.7, rat exposure of 28,766 and a 52-fold increase in cynomolgus exposure over compound 9. The same trifluoromethyl without the ortho-fluorine (14 against 9) did almost nothing, which is what makes this a real interaction between two changes rather than two independent gains.

units.title: The trifluoromethyl only works with the fluorine
units.text: Adding a fluorinated group to the amide worked spectacularly, but only because the other fluorine was already there. On its own it did nothing at all. Two changes that are worthless apart and transformative together.

units.title: A second fluorine for potency
units.text: A meta-fluorine twists the phenyl ring slightly out of plane with the azetidine, which the authors report as a consistent potency trend across related scaffolds. Enzymatic potency doubles to 0.25 nM and Caco-2 nearly doubles to 8.5.

units.title: A second fluorine for potency
units.text: A second fluorine, on the other side of the ring, twists the molecule slightly and doubles its potency. The chemists say they see the same effect across several related series and are writing it up separately.

units.title: Remove the fluorine and watch it collapse
units.text: Deleting the ortho-fluorine from 18 leaves potency untouched at 0.25 nM and takes Caco-2 from 8.5 to 1.4, rat exposure from 11,884 to 5,606 and rat bioavailability from 54 to 21 per cent. This is the control that proves the intramolecular hydrogen bond, not the fluorine's electronics, is what carries the PK.

units.title: Remove the fluorine and watch it collapse
units.text: The chemists took the key fluorine back off again. The compound was just as potent and far worse at everything else. That is how you show a hypothesis was right: undo it and watch the benefit disappear.

units.title: Shrinking the hinge binder, and paying for it
units.text: The 7H-pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidine is ubiquitous in kinase inhibitors and, being electron-rich, is prone to CYP-mediated oxidation. A bare pyrazole still binds the hinge, at 314 nM: a 1250-fold loss. The two pyrazole nitrogens make the same contacts, to the main-chain amide of Leu932 and the carbonyl of Glu930, but the smaller ring has poorer geometry and less surface to work with.

units.title: Shrinking the hinge binder, and paying for it
units.text: The part of the molecule that grips the protein was replaced with something smaller and less vulnerable to being broken down. It still gripped, in the same two places, but a thousand times more weakly. The rest of this work is buying that potency back.

units.title: One methyl, sixteen-fold
units.text: Methylating the pyrazole 3-position recovers 16-fold, to 19 nM, and doubles isoform selectivity to 48-fold.

units.title: One methyl, sixteen-fold
units.text: One methyl group on the small ring recovered sixteen-fold of the lost potency and doubled the selectivity at the same time.

units.title: The second methyl, and the drug
units.text: The 3,5-dimethylpyrazole recovers 28-fold overall to 11 nM. Against 18 it is 44-fold weaker on the enzyme and nearly twice as isoform-selective, at 46-fold, with whole blood selectivity up 2.7-fold. The prize is elsewhere: dog clearance falls from 82 to 4 per cent of hepatic blood flow, and dog oral bioavailability rises from 1 per cent to 100 per cent.

units.title: The second methyl, and the drug
units.text: The second methyl finished the job. Compared with the compound it replaced it is much weaker against the purified enzyme, more selective, and the difference that matters is in dogs: the previous compound was almost entirely destroyed before reaching the bloodstream, and this one arrives intact.

units.title: 10PI, JAK1
units.text: Povorcitinib bound to the JAK1 JH1 domain at 1.54 A. The two pyrazole nitrogens hydrogen bond the hinge: the main-chain amide of Leu932 and the main-chain carbonyl of Glu930. The molecule is longer than a conventional dual JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor, so its phenyl ring reaches towards the P-loop, which in JAK1 sits about 2 A higher than in JAK2 and opens a small lipophilic groove for the trifluoromethyl group.

units.title: 10PI, JAK1
units.text: The drug sitting in JAK1. It grips the protein at the hinge, the same place most kinase drugs bind, and reaches further than usual towards a loop that sits higher in JAK1 than in its near-twin JAK2. That extra room is the paper's explanation for why it prefers JAK1.

units.title: 10PJ, JAK2
units.text: The same compound bound to JAK2 JH1 at 1.59 A: the true twin structure, one ligand in both isoforms. The hinge contacts to Glu930 and Leu932 are conserved. The differences the authors point to are elsewhere: JAK2 has Asn859 bent towards the pocket and hydrogen bonding Glu1015, where JAK1 has His885 pointing at solvent, and JAK2's Phe860 may orient the phenyl ring into a closed disposition. The authors describe this explanation as speculative, and the app says so wherever it is shown.

units.title: 10PJ, JAK2
units.text: The very same drug molecule, in the protein it is meant to avoid. Having both pictures is unusual and valuable: the grip at the hinge is identical, and the differences are around the edges of the pocket. The chemists are careful to call their explanation a hypothesis, not a finding.

units.title: The codes are `10PI` and `10PJ`, with the digit one and the digit zero
units.text: The codes are `10PI` and `10PJ`, with the digit one and the digit zero. The paper prints them as `1OPI` and `1OPJ` in one place, which would be the letter O, and both of those are real, unrelated entries: `1OPI` is a solution structure of a U2AF65 RNA recognition motif, and `1OPJ` is the auto-inhibited form of c-Abl. Neither has anything to do with JAK. Searching RCSB for povorcitinib and for INCB054707 returns `10PI` and `10PJ`, both titled "JAK1 kinase (JH1 domain) in complex with povorcitinib" and the JAK2 equivalent, at 1.54 and 1.59 A, and both containing ligand `A1C68`, which is povorcitinib. The bundle uses the verified codes and never the letter-O forms. ## BUILD_SPEC 9.5 item 4: murine or rat? The methods say rat.

units.title:
The abstract and the conclusions say "murine arthritis models"; the model described in
   the methods is an adjuvant-induced arthritis model in RATS
units.text: The abstract and the conclusions say "murine arthritis models"; the model described in the methods is an adjuvant-induced arthritis model in RATS. The text is explicit: "the adjuvant-induced arthritis (AIA) model in rats", and the histopathology work is "an AIA rat model". Rats are not mice. The bundle and every caption in the app say rat, per BUILD_SPEC 9.5 item 4, and the paper's own wording is recorded here rather than repeated. ## The selectivity explanation is a hypothesis, and is labelled as one

units.title: The authors call their own structural explanation speculative, twice
units.text: The authors call their own structural explanation speculative, twice. The P-loop argument, JAK1's His885 pointing at solvent against JAK2's Asn859 bending into the pocket and hydrogen bonding Glu1015, plus JAK2's Phe860 closing the space, is offered as "hypothesised" and "these observations are speculative and under further investigation". The app marks every statement of it as the authors' hypothesis. This is exactly what the provenance rail is for: the data is a measurement, the explanation is a proposal, and the difference is visible.

units.title: JAK1 and JAK2 residue numbers are not equivalent
units.text: JAK1 and JAK2 residue numbers are not equivalent. Glu930 and Leu932 are the hinge in both isoforms, which is a coincidence of numbering and not an alignment; His885 and Asn859 occupy analogous positions with completely different numbers. `motifs.tsv` scopes every row to its structure with a `pdb_id` column, because without that scoping JAK1's His885 would be stamped onto whatever JAK2 happens to have at residue 885. ## KLIFS has not indexed these structures yet

units.title: JAK1 and JAK2 are kinases, but `klifs` is false for both structures in this bundle
units.text: JAK1 and JAK2 are kinases, but `klifs` is false for both structures in this bundle. KLIFS knows both kinases and has 85-position pocket definitions for them, but 10PI and 10PJ are too recently deposited to appear in its structure list, so there is no pocket mapping to fetch for these particular entries. Setting `klifs: true` would claim a pocket index the bundle does not have and leave the ruler with 85 empty affordances. The flag therefore says false, the ruler runs off the sequence exactly as it does for KRAS, and the motifs come from the hand-curated table. Nothing about the app implies a pocket numbering that is not there. When KLIFS indexes these entries the flag can be turned back on and `gc struct` will pick the mapping up with no other change. This is also why `residues with motif` is 11 here against 61 for FGFR: every motif in this bundle is hand-assigned from the paper's own text, rather than inherited from a pocket definition covering 85 positions. ## Scope

units.title: Table 3 is deliberately not in this bundle
units.text: Table 3 is deliberately not in this bundle. It lists two earlier in-house compounds, an approved c-Met inhibitor and a clinical 11-beta-HSD1 inhibitor, as precedent for the intramolecular hydrogen bonding tactic. They are not compounds of this campaign and they act on entirely different targets, so including them would put two unrelated drugs in the SAR table. The precedent itself is told in the Story.

units.title: Compounds 10 to 13 do not appear in the paper's main tables
units.text: Compounds 10 to 13 do not appear in the paper's main tables. The numbering jumps from 9 to 14 in Table 4 because 11 and 13 are the Table 3 precedent compounds. There is no gap in this bundle's data: those numbers simply belong to other molecules. ## Transcription and blanks

units.title: Table 1 is laid out with compounds as columns and assays as rows
units.text: Table 1 is laid out with compounds as columns and assays as rows , the opposite of every other table in this set, and was transcribed accordingly. Compound 4 has no whole blood, selectivity or clearance data published: those cells are empty, not zero.

units.title: Compounds 14 and 17 have incomplete cynomolgus data
units.text: Compounds 14 and 17 have incomplete cynomolgus data , and compound 14 has none at all. Empty cells stay empty.

units.title: Doses differ between rows and between tables
units.text: Doses differ between rows and between tables. Compound 9 appears in Tables 1, 2 and 4 with consistent values, and its PK rows carry different doses in different tables, so each row keeps its own dose note and no AUC is compared across rows without it.

units.title: The IL-2 T cell value is published as a range
units.text: The IL-2 T cell value is published as a range , 10 to 30 nM across pSTAT3, pSTAT5 and proliferation. It is stored as its midpoint with the range recorded in the row's note, because a range cannot be plotted and must not be silently narrowed to one end. ## Chemistry

units.title: Povorcitinib is verified twice
units.text: Povorcitinib is verified twice. Its structure matches the deposited chemical component `A1C68` found in both 10PI and 10PJ, and PubChem's povorcitinib, including the (2S) stereocentre of the trifluoropropan-2-yl amide. The Table 4, 5 and 6 series is built from that verified core by molzip, changing only the hinge binder, the two aryl fluorines and the amide substituent.

units.title: The Table 1 scaffolds (compounds 4 to 8) are figure-derived
units.text: The Table 1 scaffolds (compounds 4 to 8) are figure-derived. They appear only as a composite drawing with three shared cores and six capping groups, with no IUPAC names in the main text and no coordinates. They are flagged as such in `compounds.tsv`, and they are the least certain identities in this bundle.
